note: Official names, descriptions and grades as published on PlayStation (55 trophies: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze). Guides written for this entry; sources named beside each guide.

trophies.guide: The platinum pops automatically the moment the other 54 trophies are earned — there is no separate task. Work the roadmap in order: finish the story first so nothing time-sensitive slips past, clear the stranger strands while their givers are still around, then grind the counted activities and location sweeps, and leave the 100% completion trophy for last since it needs almost everything else done anyway. If one trophy is holding the platinum back, use the kind and grade filters in this tracker to isolate it.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this unlocks during the first hour of play with no way to miss it. Follow the on-screen objectives to the end of the mission rather than wandering off — the trophy fires when the mission-complete screen appears. Treat it as the game's tutorial: it teaches movement, driving and the fishing basics you will reuse for the Cal fishing challenge later.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Story progression trophy for finishing every mission in Chapter 1. It cannot be missed — the chapter only ends when its final mission is done. Before pushing into Chapter 2, it is worth clearing any stranger icons already on the map and trying each activity type you have unlocked, because several strand givers move or disappear as chapters advance.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Awarded for completing Chapter 2's final mission; unmissable story progression. Chapter 2 opens up more of Leonida, so use the freer stretches between missions to bank progress on the long counters — stunts, discovered vehicles and explored areas all accumulate quietly while you travel. Keep an eye on stranger strands introduced this chapter and finish them before the chapter closes.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3 to earn this one; it is tied to the chapter's last mission and cannot be missed. By this point most activity types should be unlocked, so knock out Master of None (try every activity type once) before moving on. Also start the Shooting Range gold medals early — 42 challenges is the longest single grind on the list and it is painless in short sessions between story beats.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Story trophy for wrapping up Chapter 4. Like the earlier chapter trophies it is unmissable, but Chapter 4 is a good checkpoint: after it, the endgame narrows toward the finale, so sweep any unfinished stranger strands and partner activities now while the full cast is still available. Check your tracker for missable-flagged trophies before starting the final stretch.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: One of only two golds: complete the game's final mission. Before triggering the finale, save in a separate slot and clear anything flagged missable in this guide — partner trophies and unfinished stranger strands are the usual casualties of an ending. After the credits the world stays open for cleanup, so the counted trophies (stunts, races, collectibles) can safely be finished in free roam.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Named story mission trophy: play Breakfast Run through to its completion screen. It sits on the main path, so it cannot be missed, but it is a handy early checkpoint — the mission introduces systems the later heist missions build on. If a mission fails, retry from the checkpoint rather than reloading; the trophy only needs the successful completion.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Complete The Cartel Heist story mission. Heists reward preparation, so stock up on armour and ammunition before starting and keep a manual save from before the mission in case you want to replay a cleaner run. The trophy is unmissable — it fires on the mission-complete screen — and the payout is a good seed for the money trophies (laundering and shop spending) later.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Story mission trophy for finishing Child's Play. It is on the critical path and cannot be missed. Missions like this one often contain the game's choice moments, and every choice you make feeds the Actions Speak Louder counter, so play them naturally rather than skipping cutscenes — the count only grows when choices are actually made.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Complete the Headliners mission to unlock this. Unmissable main-path trophy. Headliners-style set pieces are good places to practise Combat Focus, since scripted firefights bunch enemies together — useful rehearsal for Gunslinger, which needs five takedowns inside a single Combat Focus use.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Finish VCIA Takedown, the story mission set around the VCIA. The mission itself is unmissable, but treat the whole VCIA sequence as a window: the free-roam trophy Catch Me If You Can asks for an unscheduled departure at VCIA, and airport access can change once the story moves on. Do the VCIA free-roam trophy around this mission rather than leaving it for the endgame.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Story trophy for completing Operation Savage Glory. It cannot be missed, but operations like this one tend to be the game's longest missions, so save beforehand and go in stocked. Finishing it also tends to unlock late-game gear and areas that make the activity grinds (bank vaults, gang operations) noticeably easier.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: The second gold, and effectively the endgame: reach 100% completion on the stats screen. The percentage is fed by story missions, stranger strands, activities, collectibles and exploration, so it naturally comes last — finishing the other roadmap stages leaves only a short checklist of leftovers. Use the in-game completion breakdown to find the missing percent instead of guessing, and keep this tracker ticked as you go so the last few items are easy to spot.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Land 250 stunts across the whole playthrough. Stunts are the jumps and near-miss style feats the game registers while driving — ramps, rooftop gaps and clean landings. The counter is cumulative and never resets, so the efficient route is a fast bike and a repeatable ramp loop: find one reliable jump near a respawn point and farm it, or simply drive everywhere instead of fast-travelling and let the count build during story play. Check the stats screen to see how many you still need.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample every activity type the game offers — nine types in total, from races and the shooting range to fishing, bowling and drone racing — at least once each. You do not need to win, just start and finish (or properly attempt) each one. The activities unlock gradually through the story, so sweep the map icons after Chapter 3 when the full set is available; this trophy doubles as a tour that teaches you where the counted activity trophies live.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: The grind trophy of the list: gold medals in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Each challenge is a short timed target course, and gold demands near-perfect accuracy at speed. Work through them weapon by weapon, learn each course's target order, and restart the instant a run goes sloppy rather than finishing a doomed attempt. Short sessions between story missions keep it painless — a few golds a day clears the set long before the endgame.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 locations spread across Leonida. Drone races are checkpoint time trials flown through gates; winning means beating the target time, not just finishing. Learn a course with one slow sighting run, then attack it — most time is lost on tight turns, so brake early and keep the line smooth. Locations unlock as you explore, so pair this with the exploration trophy and clear each race when you first reach its area.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different street races — repeat wins on the same course do not count, so keep moving to new race icons as they appear. Use a fast, grippy car you know well rather than the outright fastest car you own; most losses come from crashes, not top speed. Races also pay, so this trophy quietly funds the spending and property trophies. Tick each win off in the tracker notes as you go so you do not re-run a course you have already won.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Find Cal's fishing challenge and out-fish him. Fishing is introduced in the opening mission, and the challenge is a head-to-head catch contest: cast where the fish are biting, watch the tension so the line does not snap, and favour quick, steady catches over waiting for one big fish. If Cal wins the first attempt, simply challenge him again — there is no penalty for retries and his spot stays marked.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Finish any one arcade game from start to its game-over or completion screen. Arcades are found in bars and entertainment spots around Leonida; walk up to a cabinet, play a full session, and the trophy pops when the game ends properly rather than when you walk away mid-run. It is one of the quickest trophies on the list and also counts toward trying every activity type.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Work through Andy's mission strand to its final mission. Stranger strands appear as icons on the map and each one is a short chain — the trophy only fires on the last mission of the chain, not the first. Because strand givers can move on when the story advances, complete Andy's chain promptly when it unlocks and check the map after each chapter for his next marker. Finishing this strand also counts toward the eight strands needed for Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.missable_reason: Stranger strand: Andy's missions are only offered while his strand is active, and strands can close as chapters advance — finish the strand when it appears instead of leaving it for the endgame.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's strand through to its final mission. As with every strand, only the closing mission awards the trophy, and the chain may pause between steps until the next marker appears — check the map after story missions. Do not leave Kenton half-finished: strands are the easiest trophies to strand (pun intended) by advancing the story, so clear each step as it becomes available. Counts toward Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.missable_reason: Stranger strand: Kenton's chain must be finished while his markers are active; leaving strands until after the finale risks the giver no longer being available.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's mission strand, ending with his final mission. Follow his map markers in order and complete each step as it appears — strand chains can stall if you ignore them while chapters roll on. Billy's strand is one of the eight that feed Strangers & Freaks, so a tidy habit is to clear every new strand icon the moment it shows up, then return to the story.
trophies.missable_reason: Stranger strand: Billy's final mission is only reachable while his strand is open; finish the chain before pushing deep into later chapters.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Finish eight full stranger mission strands anywhere in Leonida. The named strands for Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each have their own trophy, so completing those five gets you most of the way; three more strands from other strangers complete the set. A strand only counts when its final mission is done, so track chains, not individual missions. Because givers can disappear as the story moves, treat every new strand icon as a priority detour.
trophies.missable_reason: Needs eight finished stranger strands; strands are tied to their givers' availability, so strands left unfinished when the story ends can lock this silver away — complete strands as they unlock.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's strand through to his final mission. Follow the chain marker by marker and do not park it mid-way — strand givers are not guaranteed to wait while you finish the story. Randy's strand also counts toward the eight needed for Strangers & Freaks. If his next marker does not appear immediately, progress one story mission and check the map again; strand steps often unlock in sequence with the chapters.
trophies.missable_reason: Stranger strand: Randy's chain must be completed while his strand is active; unfinished strands are the classic missable in this list.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's mission strand, closing with his final mission. Like the other named strands, the trophy fires only on the last step, and the chain counts toward Strangers & Freaks. Strands are safest done immediately: when Tyrone's icon appears, run the chain to completion before returning to chapter missions, and keep a pre-finale save so any strand you overlooked can still be recovered.
trophies.missable_reason: Stranger strand: Tyrone's final mission requires his whole chain done while the strand is open — clear it when it appears.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots scattered across Leonida. Each spot is a scenic location where the meditate prompt appears — walk into the marked area and use it once; a short animation confirms the spot is registered. The efficient method is a region-by-region sweep: clear every spot in one district before moving on, and pair the trip with exploration and vehicle discovery so the driving does triple duty. Spots stay available in free roam, so this is safe to leave for the cleanup stage.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Take Bret's hunting request and track down the unique animal he asks for. Unique animals are one-of-a-kind spawns that only appear for this hunt — follow Bret's briefing to the hunting area, approach quietly so the animal does not bolt, and take it down cleanly with a rifle from range. If it escapes, leave the area and return to reset the spawn. Because the hunt hangs off Bret's availability, do it when his marker is active instead of saving it for last.
trophies.missable_reason: Tied to Bret's stranger request: the unique-animal hunt is offered through Bret, so do it while his strand/marker is active rather than after the story ends.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete three full collectible card sets. Cards are hidden around Leonida as pickups, and a set completes only when every card in it is found — partial sets give nothing. Sweep one district at a time and use the collection screen to see which cards of a set you still lack, then hunt the gaps. Cards remain in the world after the story, so this silver is a natural endgame cleanup task alongside meditation spots and exploration.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK It action at 100 different locations. This is a pure location sweep: each distinct spot where you perform the action counts once, so repeating it in the same place does not help. Work district by district, triggering it at landmarks, viewpoints and activity spots as you pass through for other trophies — exploration, meditation spots and drone races all drag you to fresh locations anyway. The counter is cumulative and available in free roam, so it pairs perfectly with the stage-4 cleanup.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the game's challenges — the short feat-based tasks tracked in the challenges menu (distance driven, near misses, weapon feats and similar). Open the challenges screen, sort by progress, and finish the ones you are closest to first; many complete themselves during normal play. The count is cumulative across the whole save, so check in regularly and mop up the easy leftovers in free roam rather than grinding from zero at the end.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner alongside, raise a four-star wanted level, then lose it completely and escape. Build the heat in a busy area (the shop-robbery trophy Retail Therapy is a natural way to get there), then break line of sight: swap vehicles out of view, dive into alleys or off-road, and stay hidden until the stars grey out and clear. Both of you must survive the escape — if your partner goes down, reload and retry. Do this while the story keeps the pair together.
trophies.missable_reason: Needs your partner with you: partner availability depends on the story, so earn it while the pair is together in free roam — it cannot be done solo or after story beats that split the pair.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops in a row with your partner while keeping your wanted level alive the whole time. Pick three stores close together, rob the first to start the heat, then drive straight to the next without hiding or letting the stars clear — the counter resets if the wanted level drops. Keep the route short and the car fast, and let your partner cover while you work the register. A clean run naturally leaves you at high stars, which sets up Hot Together straight afterwards.
trophies.missable_reason: Partner trophy with a twist: the wanted level must stay active across all three robberies, and it needs your partner present — do it while the pair roams together, before story beats separate them.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 distinct vehicles — getting into (or otherwise registering) a model you have not used before adds it to the count. Leonida's traffic, parked cars, boats and aircraft all feed the tally, so variety beats repetition: whenever you see a vehicle type you do not recognise, take it for a short spin. The counter is cumulative and never resets, and normal story play plus the exploration sweep will carry you most of the way; check the stats screen for the exact number remaining.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Drop five enemies during one activation of Combat Focus, the slow-time combat ability. The trick is setup: wait for a dense group — a gang operation or a story firefight with enemies bunched together — then trigger Combat Focus and chain headshots before the meter drains. A fast-firing weapon with a big magazine is more forgiving than a slow heavy hitter. If you fall one short, let the ability recharge and try the next group; there is no penalty for failed attempts.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure from the VCIA — in practice, get into the airport grounds and leave by air (or otherwise exit in a way the airport did not schedule) rather than walking out the front. The reliable window is around the VCIA Takedown story mission, when the airport is open to you; after the story moves on, access can tighten. Plan the escape route before you trigger the alarm: a fast vehicle to the runway, then out. Save before the attempt so a failed run costs nothing.
trophies.missable_reason: VCIA access is story-sensitive: the airport features in VCIA Takedown, so make the unscheduled departure around that mission window while you can still get in and out freely.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: The description is a joke, not instructions: it points at the Rhino, the game's tank. The trophy is tied to getting into and using a Rhino — military hardware that appears around bases and high-end wanted responses. The practical route is to raise enough heat (or visit military ground) until a Rhino is deployed, then take it: approach from the side, deal with the crew, and drive it away. Because the official text gives no steps, verify the exact trigger against the cited lists before a long attempt, and keep a save from before you start.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store start-to-finish without being detected — no alarm raised, no witness spotting you, no wanted stars. Approach at a quiet moment, stay out of the staff's line of sight, and work the cases quickly; the moment you are seen, the attempt is blown, so reload your save and retry rather than finishing loudly. A suppressed approach and a planned exit (vehicle parked close, facing out) make the difference. Any jewelry store qualifies, so pick the smallest one you know.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and successfully escape after each one — the escape is part of the requirement, so dying with the money does not count. Vaults are the heavy end of the robbery system: bring armour, a fast getaway car parked close, and a route that breaks line of sight quickly. Work one bank at a time and confirm the counter advanced on the stats screen before moving on. The payouts also feed the laundering and spending trophies, so bank robberies are efficient money as well as progress.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armoured truck and get away clean. Armoured trucks run regular routes through the city — spot one, block or disable it, crack the back, grab the cash and leave before the response builds. The escape matters: lose the wanted level completely for the trophy to register. A quiet stretch of road and a pre-parked fast car make this a two-minute job; if the first truck gets away, another will be along soon enough.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida — every named district and region must be visited at least once. The map fills in as you travel, so the systematic approach is to check which areas are still greyed out and drive (or fly) through each one; simply entering the area registers it. Story play covers most of the state naturally, leaving a handful of remote corners for the cleanup stage. Combine the sweep with meditation spots, WAiNK It locations and vehicle discovery to clear four counters in one road trip.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the nine gangs in Leonida. Each gang runs its own operation sites; hit one site per gang and escape with the take. Keep a checklist of which gangs you have done — the tracker note field is perfect for it — because the game does not list them for you in one place. Operations are guarded, so scout the site, thin out the guards, grab the goods and leave before reinforcements pile in. Nine gangs, one hit each, and the trophy is yours.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Head to Ocean Beach, find a bar with a view, and order a cocktail. This is a sightseeing trophy: the trigger is enjoying the drink at the right spot, so sit down at the Ocean Beach venue and use the drink prompt rather than just walking past. It takes a minute, it is available early, and it also counts toward trying every activity type. A good first trophy to bank while you are still learning the map.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Get inside a vehicle showroom, take one of the display cars, and smash your way out through the glass in classic style. The showroom floor cars are the point — driving your own car through the window is not the same thing. Pick a showroom with a street-facing glass front, line up the exit before you start the engine, and commit: the trophy registers on the smash-out, wanted stars and all. Save beforehand in case the first attempt ends in a wall instead of the street.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play bowling at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and complete a game — 'follow-through' is the hint that you need to actually bowl, not just visit. Walk in, start a game, and play it to the final frame; your score does not matter. Bowling is one of the nine activity types, so this also ticks a box for Master of None. Quick, safe, and available in free roam whenever the alley is open.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: The official text is deliberately vague — 'a partnership with mass appeal' — and the trophy is about doing something noteworthy together with your partner. Partner activities are the thread that runs through this list (the wanted-level escape and the shop robberies are both partner trophies), so the practical approach is to spend time in free roam with your partner, run partner activities together, and watch for the pop. Because it needs the pair together, do not leave it until after the finale; verify the precise trigger against the cited lists if it has not popped by the end of Chapter 4.
trophies.missable_reason: Partner trophy: the description is about the partnership, so it needs your partner present and active — earn it while the pair is together rather than after the story separates them.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Make choices — lots of them. PlayStation tracks a counter for this trophy that runs to 500, fed by the decision moments scattered through missions and encounters. There is no single trick: play through the story making the choices as they come, talk to people, take the optional branches, and do not skip encounter prompts. Because many choice moments are one-time story beats, a rushed playthrough that avoids optional content can end short — if the counter stalls, free-roam encounters and side activities are where the remaining choices hide.
trophies.missable_reason: Choice counter: choices are made inside missions and encounters, many of them one-time — a playthrough that skips optional encounters can finish short of the tracked count, so engage with choice moments as they appear.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: 'Second time's the charm' — succeed at something on your second attempt after failing the first. The natural reading is a retry trophy: fail an attempt, then complete it on the immediate retry. The safest way to earn it deliberately is to pick a repeatable challenge, fail the first run on purpose (or let it fail naturally), and then win the retry straight away. Keep a manual save before set-piece attempts so a first-try success does not lock you out of the pattern, and check the cited lists for the confirmed trigger if it does not pop early.
trophies.missable_reason: Reads as a retry trophy: succeed at something on the second attempt. If the trigger is a specific one-time event, a first-try success (or never retrying) can miss it — keep a save before set-piece attempts.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: Witness something strange. The description is a reaction, not an instruction, which points at one of Leonida's oddball random events or hidden encounters — the kind of thing you stumble into while exploring rather than a marked activity. The practical route is thorough exploration: remote areas, odd landmarks and night-time wandering are where strange events live. Since the official text gives no steps, cross-check the cited trophy lists for the confirmed event and location before a dedicated hunt, and explore at night when you sweep the map for the exploration trophy.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by: from a moving vehicle, lean out and strike a pedestrian (or rider) with a melee attack so they go down like a bowling pin. A motorcycle or open vehicle makes the swing easiest — ride slowly past a lone target on a quiet street, time the swing as you pass, and keep rolling to avoid a crowd turning hostile. It takes a couple of attempts to judge the range; a slow pass beats a fast one every time.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 worth of marked bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from heists and robberies; your contacts convert them to clean money at a cut, and the trophy counts the total laundered, not what you keep. The efficient loop is the robbery circuit — bank vaults and gang operations pay the most marked bills — laundering after every score instead of hoarding. The counter is cumulative, so steady robbery income across the playthrough reaches the quarter-million without a dedicated grind.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in total across all shops — clothing, weapons, vehicle customisation and consumables all count toward the same running total. You will spend a good chunk naturally on weapons and armour, so the trophy usually completes itself if you buy gear instead of scavenging. If you reach the endgame short of the target, vehicle customisation is the fastest legal way to burn money: a few fully-kitted cars close the gap quickly. The spending total is cumulative and tracked on the stats screen.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Buy all eight garage properties across Leonida. Garages are purchasable safehouses for storing vehicles; each one is a property icon on the map with a price tag. The total cost is steep, so this is an endgame trophy funded by the robbery circuit — bank vaults and laundered marked bills. Buy them one by one as money allows and tick each off here; owned garages also make the vehicle-discovery and stunt grinds easier by giving you storage in every district.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register ten vehicles in the Scooter Bros app. Open the app on your in-game phone and register vehicles you own — each distinct vehicle you add counts once. You need ten registered vehicles, so this pairs naturally with buying and storing cars in your garages: register each new acquisition as you buy it. If you are short, cheap vehicles count just as well as supercars, so a handful of budget purchases finishes the set without touching your savings.
trophies.name: On the Spot
